+## C-009 — Export the captured calculation and preserve deliberate input
+
+A local download uses the exact immutable SDK JSON captured with the displayed
+full chart. It never recalculates on click or reconstructs missing fields from a
+positions-only summary. Input, run and profile-access fences apply both when
+capturing and when clicking. Optional module loading may fall back before any
+natal calculation; a calculation or serialization failure never retries through
+the legacy path. Signed fixed-offset zones, inconsistent resolver context and
+known exact poles preserve established chart behavior with explicit receipt
+unavailability until their separate contracts support truthful export.
+
+The file includes sensitive birth details and chart data. Say so in all six
+locales, use a generic filename, release the local Blob URL and claim initiation
+only. This activates neither account sync nor the optional saved-record store.
+
+Russian shared-chart review reproduced the custom interaction directive replaying
+untouched SSR blanks over initialized birth details. Keep the receipt fence and
+correct replay: preserve explicit edits (including a return to blank/default) and
+eventless native edits, while untouched fields accept component initialization.
+Native reset semantics on a detached control determine defaults; selected values,
+not old option indexes, survive hydration reordering. Existing lazy activation,
+queued submit, takeover, retries and eagerHash:false behavior remain unchanged.
+
+Receipt factoring moves ephemeris code into a shared static dependency. Count the
+entire full-entry closure once under the existing 25 KB limit; do not raise any
+budget or require all markers in the entry shim. Inspect actual decoded literal
+module-loading syntax so inert provenance strings are permitted while concrete
+vendor imports, escapes, transparent parentheses and CDN targets are rejected.
+This is a bounded regression checker, not arbitrary JavaScript data-flow proof.

+# Local calculation receipt export — author implementation choices
+
+## Scope and identities
+
+The 14-file receipt patch is Freeze 2, based on site c761a49c55d125bca48ff38d81b0a9ff6fd5adcf. The separately frozen two-file interaction correction is Interaction Freeze 1. Their identity JSON files enumerate every source/test SHA-256 and patch digest. The author worked only in /private/tmp/zodiacs-platform-site-receipt-export; the root agent owns integration, release gates and delivery.
+
+## Receipt boundary and privacy
+
+The full calculator lazily loads a small calculator-receipt helper after the existing engine loader. It calculates a native chart once through delivered computePortableChart, uses that same calculation for the existing site chart, and serializes the validated existing SDK envelope once. Unknown-time Sun/Moon endpoint checks remain separate existing computeBodies operations. The download click never calculates again. Optional helper import failure falls back before natal execution; an execution or serialization failure never triggers a second calculation.
+
+The helper captures actual local date/time, resolved zone spelling and offset, arithmetic gap shift and explicit known/unknown reference. The existing unknown-time flow deliberately uses local 12:00; its receipt says local-noon. Source instant and provenance remain absent/null because the calculator does not have those claims. Local midnight arithmetic uses setUTCFullYear, preserving years 0–99. No new Intl resolution, guessed offset, fixed one-hour gap, fake zone, rounded historical seconds or synthesized provenance is introduced.
+
+Known unsupported receipt inputs are admitted to the existing chart before natal calculation but do not offer a receipt: signed fixed-offset zone strings accepted by current Intl/link parsing, known-time exact poles, and truthful civil gap-shift/flag disagreement or a negative shift. The interface gives a concise localized unavailable note. This narrow preservation path neither changes the SDK codec nor exports an envelope with dropped civil context.
+
+Receipt bytes are an immutable string bound to the committed chart object, run ID, input revision and applicable profile-access generation. Input edits synchronously clear the state and ref; new runs, positions-only imports, profile scrub and unmount also invalidate it. The click repeats the fences before creating a Blob. A legacy or positions-only summary never gains an invented historical receipt. A fresh calculation from real saved birth inputs is a new calculation, subject to the same fences.
+
+The existing result More actions disclosure contains a keyboard-accessible local JSON action using existing styles and six locale catalogs. Its label identifies a calculation receipt, and its privacy note explicitly says the file includes sensitive birth details and chart data. The generic filename includes no name, local record ID or owner ID. A synchronous anchor click preserves the user gesture; finally blocks remove the anchor and schedule URL revocation, including failure paths. Allocation/download failure has fixed localized wording. A browser download event establishes initiation, not durable filesystem persistence, and the UI claims no save success.
+
+There are no added analytics, network/storage services, SDK/store activation, account APIs, root guides, global styles/navigation, canonical Registry or Astrofolio edits. Existing save/share and ownership behavior remain intact.
+
+## Interaction replay correction
+
+The real Russian shared-chart flow exposed an existing replay boundary: client:interaction captured untouched SSR blank fields, shared-link initialization filled them, then replay dispatched the old blanks as edits. The receipt fence correctly prevented an obsolete download. Weakening that fence or changing the route hydration policy was rejected.
+
+The correction tracks dirty controls explicitly. A first-hydration recapture merges prior dirty marks so a deliberate edit back to empty/default remains intentional. A detached clone reset with native form semantics detects eventless autofill and normalized defaults without changing live controls. Only dirty controls are replayed; untouched controls admit shared/profile initialization. Tracking continues through takeover, failed hydrate retries retain captured edits, and queued submissions still wait for commit barriers. Single-select value behavior is retained; multiple selected values use values rather than old option indexes so reordered options cannot change the selected value. The fixed eagerHash:false policy, intent/fallback scheduling, retry behavior and timeout-backed hidden-tab barrier remain unchanged.
+
+The first replay draft used selected-option indexes; independent real Chrome review demonstrated wrong selection when hydration reordered options. That draft and reproduction remain evidence. The frozen correction uses stable values and passes the same independent negative controls. This correction is separately reviewable from the 14 receipt files.
+
+## Explicit unresolved work
+
+Sixteen historical minute-resolution counterexamples remain a pre-existing shared resolver defect, including America/Manaus 1914-01-01 00:00 resolving four seconds forward without dst-gap. Adjacent false-fold flags also require a separate numerical correction. The receipt boundary preserves existing chart behavior and refuses the inconsistent civil receipt; it does not certify the resolver.
+
+Signed fixed-offset receipt syntax and exact-pole angle coverage remain declared SDK receipt limitations. Active richer saved-record lifecycle, durable cross-tab owner revocation/erasure, account integration, migration, publication, production deployment and external adoption are outside this slice. Root owns the bundle-gate correction needed for the real static full-engine closure; the author did not weaken the gate.

+The first frozen bundle-gate candidate has unresolved concrete loader-detection defects. Static closure accounting passed the independently exercised cases, and every fixture retained the exact original `budgets.json` bytes.
+
+1. `hasExternalEphemerisImport` skips AST parsing unless the raw source includes `astronomy-engine`. Valid JavaScript escaped module specifiers therefore bypass the new AST detector. Actual subprocess examples returning success: `import "astronomy-\u0065ngine"`, `export * from "\u0061stronomy-engine"`, `import("astronomy-\x65ngine")`, and `require("astronomy-\u0065ngine")`. The AST decodes these to the forbidden package name, so remove the raw substring prefilter. Root has accepted this correction.
+2. Transparent parentheses around literal arguments or the require callee bypass the detector: `import(("astronomy-engine"))`, `require(("astronomy-engine"))`, and `(require)("astronomy-engine")`. All three were rejected by the old gate's marker check but pass the first frozen candidate. Unwrap `ParenthesizedExpression` nodes before the concrete loader/literal checks; this requires no arbitrary data-flow evaluation.
+3. Explicit external vendor URLs now pass: `import "https://esm.sh/astronomy-engine@2.1.19"` and `import("https://esm.sh/astronomy-engine")`. These are syntactically concrete module targets, and the old gate rejected them. Root must retain or explicitly redefine this external-vendor boundary; it is distinct from inert receipt metadata.
+
+The candidate correctly rejects concrete commented imports and rejects eagerly reachable engine fingerprints through commented static side-effect imports, escaped local chunk specifiers and re-exports. A cyclic shared closure is measured without recursion failure or double counting. A full closure re-exporting two individually small high-entropy chunks correctly fails the unchanged 25 KB engine limit.
+
+Two boundaries are deliberately distinguished from these correction requests. The unchanged source regex misses a side-effect import with whitespace in an unexpected source file; this is an existing limitation, not a newly introduced regression. The source's existing named-import allowlist check still rejects the corresponding named import. Arbitrary aliased/computed module-loading targets are not a complete data-flow or execution-security boundary, and this review does not demand a JavaScript security verifier. Dynamic imports are excluded from the static closure by definition; static reachability alone does not prove that all dynamic loading waits for interaction. Native export/hydration checks remain independent work.
+
+Evidence is actual Node 22.23.2 subprocess execution of physically copied frozen gate code using a physically copied TypeScript runtime. `initial-results.json` retains the first six controls, `adversarial-results.json` retains the next seventeen controls, and all fixture trees and stdout/stderr logs remain under `fixtures/`. Old-gate comparisons put both fingerprints directly in `full.*.js` so the original fingerprint rule is satisfied; the old gate's inert-name rejection is deliberately observable. No vendor fixture was executed as browser/module code, and no network request was made.
+
+No product or budget file was edited. Acceptance is pending a new root freeze and targeted rerun of the concrete failures.

+# Independent Freeze 2 review — blocked on hydration replay
+
+Reviewed candidate: receipt export patch SHA256 `d6639f7bd46ed9adce30c1d1f374394356350593234dacdcc82baa20086fa425`, based on `c761a49c55d125bca48ff38d81b0a9ff6fd5adcf`. Fourteen frozen files are copied and hashed in `freeze2-source/` and `freeze2-identity.json`. This review did not modify product source, accounts, saved data, remote repositories, or production. Browser data is synthetic.
+
+Freeze 2 is not accepted as a complete consumer feature. Actual Russian full shared input yields a chart but no receipt because existing interaction hydration replay restores untouched blank date/time controls and dispatches edit events after the shared calculation begins. The revision guard correctly discards that now-stale receipt. Author and reviewer independently reproduce the behavior. The author separately traced replayControls through native logpoints. Our `ru-diagnostic-observation.json` records one calculator, one computed event, empty date/time controls, a correct prior result, and native disabled=true. Do not weaken the receipt guard to repair this failure.
+
+## Executed independent browser evidence
+
+27 acceptance groups passed across the original, targeted, post-natal, and native zoom runners. Actual static build pages execute in owned Chrome 152 contexts, with pinned Node 22.23.2, served-file hashes, requests, page errors, synthetic storage observations, actual downloaded files, and Chrome precise coverage for exact public/native natal function identities.
+
+- Eight truthful receipt fixtures cover ordinary known time, one-hour gap and fold, 30-minute gap, whole skipped date at unknown local noon, historical LMT, requested Placidus actual whole-house polar fallback, and ordinary unknown local noon. Files parse through the pinned receipt codec; no invented source instant, name or place label.
+- Three bounded preservation controls retain one existing legacy calculation and show receipt unavailable before public natal execution: signed offset, a four-second historical resolver mismatch, and known exact geographic pole.
+- Stale retained DOM click after an edit cannot download; a subsequent successful run exports different bytes for its own inputs.
+- Positions-only import presents its existing reduced surface without the receipt helper or any natal computation.
+- English, Spanish, Portuguese, French and Italian keyboard downloads work at 390 CSS pixels without horizontal overflow. Russian is the unresolved blocker above.
+- Full, moon, and rising idle/focus routes do not fetch the receipt helper.
+- A real delayed helper request plus an input edit cannot publish a receipt for the old input revision.
+- A real failed optional helper request preserves the chart using exactly one native legacy call and no public natal call.
+- A synthetic owner profile handoff exercises the actual read guard and profile-access event. Revoking its controlled canRead policy while the helper request is pending clears the profile-derived input/result and performs zero natal calls. This is lifecycle-boundary verification, not authentication or deployed account-policy certification.
+- A controlled JSON.stringify fault limited to the actual natal-envelope schema after an earlier success causes the next requested run to fail after exactly one native/public natal call. There is no fallback recalculation, stale download, or raw exception exposure. This is explicit fault injection, not natural storage exhaustion or device failure.
+- Actual Chrome default zoom set to approximately four (not CSS zoom or page-scale emulation): 320 CSS pixel viewport, DPR4, document/body CSS zoom1, scrollWidth320, focused receipt button fully visible, valid keyboard download. Original zoom1 restored, owned context closed, screenshot visually inspected.

+## Harness errors retained honestly
+
+The first positions-only assertion incorrectly expected no `.calc__result`, although the existing reduced surface deliberately uses that class. The corrected case asserts `[data-positions-only]`, absence of the download button/helper, and zero native/public natal calls. Initial result/log/screenshot are retained and are not a product defect.

The rerun allows only a 1e-12 representation tolerance and verifies actual 320 CSS px/DPR4 metrics. Both harness versions/results are preserved.
+
+## Limits and next acceptance
+
+Finite native Chromium verification does not certify all browsers, all IANA history, astronomical accuracy, account lifecycle activation, SDK publication, deployment, or external adoption. Existing historical resolver inconsistencies and exact-pole receipt coverage remain explicit limitations; root owns the separate SDK seconds correction. The author owns the newly coordinated hydration replay correction. Review its frozen source and native cases before claiming receipt export ready. Root owns final integration, full checks, bundle policy and delivery records.

The first zoom check expected exact floating-point four, while Chrome returned `3.9999999999999996`; it failed before page navigation. Only a 1e-12 representation tolerance was added, and native 320px/DPR4 measurements remain required. Neither is a product defect.

+## Scope and remaining qualifications
+
+The source keeps one calculation-to-receipt capture, immutable serialized download bytes, revision/run/access checks, fixed failure text, and dynamic helper isolation. Positions-only imports cannot invent a receipt. Existing save/share/profile behavior is preserved, and this slice does not activate the separately version-owned saved-record store.
+
+Signed host offset zones, inconsistent historical resolver gap context, and known exact-pole cases keep their established chart calculation with an explicit unavailable receipt. No invented zone, dropped context, rounded-away shift, post-natal retry, broadened SDK acceptance, or weakened stale guard is used. Unknown and near-pole positive controls remain eligible.
+
+The independently reproduced existing historical seconds/false-fold and local-date-endpoint concerns are numerical follow-ups, not fixed by this UI slice. Root owns the separately delivered SDK seconds correction and endpoint tracking. This finite Chromium review does not certify all browser engines, all IANA history, broad astronomical accuracy, deployed authentication, full account lifecycle erasure, or release publication. Author unit/strict/Astro and native fixture checks are attributable to the author's evidence; root owns the full integrated suite and bundle policy review.

It stays noindex during review and uses the existing site shell, artwork, Registry, disclosures, origin receipts and address parser.

The browser checks fresh same-origin Registry bytes against the reviewed SHA-256. Malformed input, wrong or unsupported network, an unknown identifier, changed source bytes and unavailable sources have distinct outcomes; failure or editing the input clears an earlier match. Pasted identifiers stay out of requests, URLs and persistent storage. Solana comparison is case-sensitive; Base comparison explicitly checks hexadecimal-byte membership without asserting mixed-case checksum validation or SDK parity.

The static page and embedded machine facts come from one local evidence adapter. Ten qualified claims distinguish public records, operator attestations, unresolved rights, contradictory sources and the platform candidate. Rebuilding never refreshes an observation date. A match establishes Registry membership, with visible limits on safety, endorsement and holder-rights implications.

### Review and evidence

- [Application preview](https://zodiacs-lkqoi56y1-zodiacsofficial.vercel.app/registry/verify/): Vercel READY at `4704acc5c7a0625dedd7601009b9c17207892ba9`, protected by Vercel login. The final anonymous browser reached that login; protected remote product scenarios remain unverified. The later delivery commit adds only documentation, test harness options and evidence.
- Node 22.23.2: full build and repository check passed (zero errors/warnings, eleven existing hints). **4,484 tests in 406 files passed**, including 75 new scoped tests. Three unrelated five-second timeouts in the first concurrent run are preserved; the final two-worker run passed without weakening timeouts.
- **11/11 local Chromium scenarios passed**: desktop/mobile320/390, contrast, keyboard/copy, no-JS facts, network/storage privacy, source tampering/failure, cancellation and real service-worker offline behavior. Six pre-existing shared shell assets miss offline; exact diagnostics remain in the evidence.
- Twenty source-grounded answer fixtures: identifiers correct and no invented rights/endorsements. **14/20 met all reviewed requirements**; five citation gaps and two omitted qualifications (overlapping counts) are preserved. Checker-source links were added; answers were not rerun. This does not establish organic discovery or independent certification.

[Checkpoint, exact commands, SHAs, logs and captures](https://github.com/ZodiacsOfficial/site/blob/codex/astrofolio-verification/docs/astrofolio-trust/STATUS.md) · [Desktop capture](https://github.com/ZodiacsOfficial/site/blob/codex/astrofolio-verification/docs/astrofolio-trust/evidence/verification-1280-hero.png) · [Mobile capture](https://github.com/ZodiacsOfficial/site/blob/codex/astrofolio-verification/docs/astrofolio-trust/evidence/verification-390-hero.png) · [Material evidence gaps](https://github.com/ZodiacsOfficial/site/blob/codex/astrofolio-verification/docs/astrofolio-trust/EVIDENCE-GAPS.md)

### Integration hold

Only `src/pages/registry/verify/**`, `src/registry/astrofolio-verification/**`, `tests/astrofolio-verification/**` and `docs/astrofolio-trust/**` are changed. Engine, SDK, API, developer-platform, canonical sources, package/configuration and shared site files stay outside this workstream. Refreshed platform PR #415 and #417 file lists have zero owned-file overlap; the SDK #6 hold is unchanged.

**Build & Check CI currently fails at the existing Phase 1 scope guard for the one new Registry route.** The guard is unchanged. Two small, unapplied [integration patches](https://github.com/ZodiacsOfficial/site/blob/codex/astrofolio-verification/docs/astrofolio-trust/integration/README.md) are reserved for the primary session: the exact-base route allowance and one contextual Registry link. Both pass `git apply --check`. The primary integrator must reconcile the allowance with the actual integration base, apply accepted shared changes, regenerate the Registry hub when adding its link, and rerun CI.

Independent entity/rights provenance, applicable holder grants and the scope of economic interests/control remain unresolved; the page says so. Keep this draft and its noindex policy until integration review. No production merge, deployment or package publication was performed.

+# Saved natal persistence author evidence — Freeze 1
+
+This is an optional callable primitive, implemented and focused-tested in an
+isolated checkout. It is not active in the product, not a completed account
+lifecycle, not a numerical accuracy certification, and not a publication or
+deployment. The integrator owns full site checks and delivery. No UI, account
+server/API, existing Living Chart database, v1 behavior, dependencies, service
+configuration, or separate Astrofolio work was changed by this author.
+
+## Exact source
+
+Base site commit: `dcc4e437a99f812666cd19dc85e6d781dbb3bedc`. Author checkout:
+`/private/tmp/zodiacs-platform-saved-record`. Four added profile-domain files
+are listed with SHA-256 in `freeze1-identity.json`; `freeze1-source.patch` applies
+on that source base. Patch SHA-256:
+`5d61510dec09e42ad2196c173da5a88f206a85af5809a27562b1daf0cc2f83a5`.
+No implementation edits followed that freeze. `identity.json` and `source.patch`
+are byte-identical convenience copies, not another revision. The identity's
+“pending independent review” field describes the time of freeze and is retained
+unchanged rather than rewritten retrospectively.
+
+The SDK is the actual existing `@zodiacs/engine` 0.1.1-rc.5 artifact, SHA-256
+`1809c1686843a6be148eb185535e32059a20c35896e29ccfc7583a6b2738da65`.
+Its existing receipt codec is the sole inner-envelope validator. Frozen local
+metadata and the validated serialized receipt are immutable strings/scalars.
+Export returns only the exact stored SDK envelope string.
+
+## Final focused verification
+
+`freeze1-runs.json` records command argument arrays, log names, and zero exit
+statuses. Runtime: pinned Node 22.23.2; Vitest 3.2.6.
+
+- `freeze1-focused-tests.log`: 74 tests passed in four files: 17 record tests,
+  32 store tests, 21 existing portable-calculation tests, and four existing
+  v1 upload-preparation tests.
+- `freeze1-typecheck.log`: strict TypeScript with the existing Node and Astro
+  ambient types passed without source suppressions.
+- `freeze1-tracked-diff-check.log`: `git diff --check` passed after the four new
+  files were marked intent-to-add. Earlier untracked checks are retained but
+  are not used as evidence of whitespace review for those new files.
+
+Coverage includes exact unlabeled and labeled SDK export; requested Placidus
+versus actual fallback and explicit Whole Sign; unknown time at 08:30 with source
+spelling preserved; receipt snapshot before a storage wait; owner partition;
+40-record atomic capacity; fresh UUID collision without overwrite; immutable
+metadata; malformed/corrupt/future record distinctions; explicit delete and
+owner clear; reentrant authority, ABA epoch, precommit and postcommit revocation;
+quota, abort and version errors; failure privacy; and no eager activation.
+The actual exported legacy `selfChartPutWire` rejects this richer record
+structurally; no legacy helper or artificial downgrade path was changed.
+
+The test memory adapter is a deterministic contract model, not evidence of
+native browser locking. The independent reviewer separately reported 22 of 22
+actual Chrome 152 checks passing against Freeze 1 on 2026-09-08. Those include
+real IndexedDB transactions, prompt cancellation while a native deletion remains
+blocked, late connection cleanup, precommit abort with no row, postcommit stale
+with a committed row, concurrent capacity, future v10 rows, terminal clear, and
+a bounded browser quota control. Its report and raw results are a separate
+review package; no duplicate author browser run or invented independent signoff
+is claimed here.
+
+## Preserved failures and corrections
+
+1. `initial-record-tests.log` retains the first 17-test run: six failed and
+   eleven passed. Unlabeled rows were incorrectly rejected because the draft
+   counted six mandatory fields rather than five. Future schema rows with
+   changed layouts were also classified corrupt; a draft regular expression
+   omitted versions such as v10. Fix: exact five/six-field v1 shape and future
+   discriminator recognition before current-layout validation. Initial source
+   copies are retained under `initial-source/`.
+2. The suspected UUID/owner trailing-newline weakness was disproved by the
+   initial tests, which already passed LF, CR, CRLF, space, and line-separator
+   controls. It is not claimed as a fixed defect. The legacy UUID helper stayed
+   unchanged; this module explicitly requires canonical 36-character IDs.
+3. `initial-store-tests.log` retains the first 47-test pass.
+4. `initial-typecheck.log` retains a command-configuration failure in an existing
+   transitive `ImportMeta.env` reference. The focused invocation omitted Astro
+   ambient types. The corrected strict invocation includes `astro/client`; no
+   source type suppression or weakening was added.
+5. `focused-tests.log`, `focused-typecheck.log`, and `focused-runs.json` retain a
+   74-test pass before the delayed-open liveness regression was strengthened.
+6. `initial-late-open-stall.log` retains the strengthened delayed-open control:
+   one test timed out after five seconds, with 31 unrelated tests skipped. The
+   caller waited for a native open event after revoke.
+   `pre-open-cancellation-store.ts.log` captures that source. Fix: track and
+   reject the logical open promise immediately while leaving settled/generation
+   guards to abort upgrades and close native handles that arrive later. The
+   final regression now requires stale settlement before emitting late success.
+   The reviewer independently retained a real-Chrome early-draft reproduction
+   under its `pre-freeze-open-review` evidence; that is distinct from its final
+   Freeze 1 acceptance.
+
+## Remaining integration boundaries
+
+The caller supplies owner identity and an epoch plus a current-authority reader.
+This is an application access-policy boundary, not authentication, encryption,
+or an origin security sandbox. A handle cannot discover or create ownership.
+Records intentionally have no revision/updatedAt/rename/overwrite/import-ID
+path. Every create uses a fresh UUID, and no semantic deduplication is attempted.
+
+Clear invalidates only its handle and completes one owner-scoped transaction.
+Another same-owner handle or tab can create later; this is explicitly tested.
+A real account/full-device erase and no-resurrection guarantee need durable
+generations/tombstones and a coordinated active lifecycle. A stale result after
+commit exposes no record or success and says `mayHaveCommitted: true`; retry is
+never automatic. Failed clear consumes the handle, so retry needs fresh explicit
+authority. Unknown storage schemas are preserved. Reads and creates preserve
+corrupt/future records; explicit known-key delete or owner clear may erase them.
+
+Active use still needs asynchronous inventory/presence and ownership handoff,
+guest ownership, import and retention policy, account export and deletion,
+clear/retry coordination, and full-device cleanup. The current fixed-key and
+synchronous lifecycle paths must not be treated as complete support for this
+new database.

+# Author implementation choices
+
+Base: site dcc4e437a99f812666cd19dc85e6d781dbb3bedc, isolated checkout.
+Read reviewer DESIGN.md and actual existing Living Chart/native-IDB counterexample
+before authoring. These choices narrow the optional primitive; no active app
+lifecycle, account policy or v1 behavior is changed.
+
+- Immutable outer record: schema, ownerKey, generated UUID, createdAt, optional
+  bounded label, and SDK envelopeJson. No revision, updatedAt, rename, supplied
+  create ID, overwrite, deduplication, wrapper import or legacy projection.
+- Bound authority is explicit ownerKey plus a safe nonnegative epoch and a
+  required reader of the current owner/epoch. This is caller application policy,
+  not authentication. The handle never discovers or creates ownership.
+- Separate IndexedDB zodiacs-saved-natal-v1/version1; records has compound
+  [ownerKey,id] key and ownerKey index. Validate existing layout without upgrades
+  or repair. Unsupported physical versions/layouts are preserved.
+- Create snapshots the existing SDK envelope before awaiting IDB. The SDK is the
+  only inner envelope validator. Label preserves supplied text, bounded to 120
+  Unicode code points and 512 UTF-8 bytes; empty/whitespace-only/control text is
+  invalid. It is local metadata and never included in envelope export.
+- Record cap40 and insertion are one readwrite transaction. Reads request at
+  most41 values; corruption/future records are errors, not empty success. Immutable
+  deletion by explicit owner/id is idempotent and can remove an unsupported record
+  at that exact known key; clear is explicit owner erasure without parsing content.
+- Track native transactions. Revoke invalidates generation and calls abort before
+  closing handles. Resolve reads and writes only after transaction completion,
+  and check authority/generation before, inside and after asynchronous boundaries.
+- Clear consumes the handle: abort/invalidate previous operations, run an
+  authorized owner-scoped transaction, then remain revoked even on failure.
+  Retry requires a new explicit handle. Other handles/tabs are separately
+  serialized by IDB but not globally revoked by this primitive.
+- Fixed result unions separate missing, denied/stale, invalid/corrupt/unsupported,
+  full/collision, quota, blocked, abort and unavailable storage. A stale write
+  after native commit reports mayHaveCommitted; no automatic retry or success
+  notification. Returned records are frozen immutable strings/scalars.
+
+- Native IndexedDB open requests cannot be cancelled. Keep a separate logical
+  cancellation callback: revoke rejects waiting callers immediately, aborts an
+  active upgrade transaction when possible, and closes any late successful
+  connection using settled/generation guards. An external blocked delete must
+  not keep the caller waiting after its authority has been revoked.
+- Terminal clear cleanup invokes revoke after its final authority check, so a
+  connection opened solely for clear cannot remain cached on a consumed handle.
+
+Rejected options: reusing/upgrading Living Chart storage would change its version
+contract; aggregate localStorage would inherit the demonstrated lost-save race;
+caller IDs/overwrites/metadata CAS would add conflict semantics without a needed
+mutable record; automatic semantic dedup would conflate distinct calculations;
+legacy receipt reconstruction would invent evidence. None is part of this slice.

+# Independent native IndexedDB review plan
+
+Status: harness prepared against the author's declared API; acceptance awaits a
+frozen, hashed patch. No product files edited. The constructor is owner/epoch
+bound; required readAuthority is application policy, not authentication.
+
+Run in isolated headless Chrome contexts against copied frozen modules and the
+exact rc.5 package, with no user browser, account, local site data or network
+service. Each native case gets a fresh context. Keep raw failures and fixes.
+
+1. Import has zero database opens. An ordinary no-label record can create, read
+   and export; missing is distinct from error. Export excludes outer metadata.
+2. Two independent native connections race at the 40-record cap; one insertion
+   succeeds and one returns full. Distinct permitted records cannot be lost.
+3. Revocation inside readAuthority itself is detected after that callback returns;
+   no stale success and no database work. Test both callback and returned-field
+   getter revocation. A→B→A with changed epoch cannot resurrect a handle.
+4. Inject revocation from a real native add request's success event before
+   transaction commit. The actual transaction must abort, not merely close.
+5. Revoke from a transaction complete listener registered before the production
+   listener. A committed row can remain under its captured owner, but the caller
+   receives stale without private data and mayHaveCommitted true.
+6. Real pending open: hold a v1 connection, queue a blocked database deletion,
+   queue the subject open behind it, revoke, then unblock. A late success must
+   close its handle. Fixed open(version1) cannot naturally upgrade an existing
+   version0 DB; do not fabricate a native upgrade-blocked event claim.
+7. Real native abort and CDP storage quota override where supported: distinguish
+   confirmed rollback from possibly committed; preserve any unsupported quota
+   control honestly rather than relabeling a synthetic error as native quota.

+   malformed envelope, future SDK required feature, and over-cap data. list/get

+   owner field differing from its physical primary key; test corrupt key/index
+   schemas as unsupported storage, not invented impossible native rows.

+   the new namespace. Preserve existing legacy helper source.

+    distinct; reads/export/delete do not affect another owner.

+    connection. Its transaction is owner scoped; another same-owner handle can
+    create afterward. Record this declared limit rather than falsely certifying
+    account erasure. Durable global clear needs a later lifecycle coordinator.

+    blocked/late requests cannot retain an unreachable connection.
